findings.title: Manifest-absent 'un-gated' verdict decided locally (partial second owner)
findings.question: ownership
findings.evidence: finish-check.mjs manifest-absent shortcut vs esk-genesis --check exit 1 for absent; both BLOCK (no behavioural divergence).
findings.resolution: fixed (author): kept as a spawn-avoidance optimization with a clearer message, plus a comment stating it must track esk-genesis's exit-1 'manifest/workflow absent = un-gated' definition; present-manifest drift stays delegated to the one owner.

findings.title: Coverage inherits the loop-safety escalation allow after the block cap
findings.question: error-handling
findings.evidence: after ESK_BLOCK_CAP consecutive blocks the turn is allowed to end with coverage still unmet, reported in the escalation note.
findings.resolution: accepted / waived by author: intentional and consistent with every other finish-check step (loop safety so a stuck agent is not wedged); ADR-0116 documents it as the honest ceiling (a loud, recorded 'shipped ungated' escalation, not a silent pass).

findings.title: Executes the consumer repo's own esk-genesis copy (prefer-own resolution)
findings.question: ownership
findings.evidence: genesisScript prefers <root>/.claude/skills/bootstrap/scripts/esk-genesis.mjs, else the installed sibling; spawn is safe (argument array, no shell, no string from file content).
findings.resolution: accepted / waived by author: deliberate so the verdict matches what the repo's own CI would show (ADR-0116 topology note); within the threat model (an attacker who can write that path can equally forge the markers/manifest).

findings.title: Upstream self-exclusion was a single-file path heuristic
findings.question: ownership
findings.evidence: existsSync(always-on/enterprise-skills-always-on.md) alone would skip any repo that hand-copied that file; not exploitable in normal flows (esk-init/genesis never mirror always-on/ into a consumer).
findings.resolution: fixed (author): tightened to require BOTH the directive and emit-directive.mjs (the pair esk-init's root-walk uses), so a stray single-file copy cannot exempt a consumer.
